title: Chinese Characters & Writing
description: Start writing Simplified Chinese: 30 characters, short lessons, stroke animations and gentle practice. An introductory pilot toward beginner learning.

lessons.title: Before you write
lessons.summary: Pinyin, tones, strokes, grids and the practice loop.

blocks.text: Start with the character, meaning and audio. Watch the stroke model, trace it, copy it, then try recall. Reading, guided writing and independent writing are separate skills.

Pinyin writes Mandarin sounds using Latin letters. Tone marks show high-level (ā), rising (á), dipping (ǎ), and falling (à) tones. An unmarked syllable may be neutral. Listen to the character audio; pronunciation can change in words.

Basic strokes include horizontal, vertical, left falling, right falling, dot, turn and hook. A turn or hook can be part of one continuous stroke. Common patterns include top before bottom and left before right; use the model for each character rather than treating these patterns as exception-free rules.

blocks.title: Comfortable practice
blocks.text: Use a finger, stylus or mouse. Trace with a faint model, then copy, then recall. There is no timer. The numbered stroke activity offers a non-drawing alternative. Progress is practice information, not an exam score.

blocks.title: A beginner pilot
blocks.text: These 30 characters introduce writing and useful vocabulary. They contribute toward beginner learning; this is not a complete A1–A2 course. Extra characters in words and examples are recognition-only unless listed in the trainer.

lessons.title: Numbers 1–5

blocks.text: Read and write five everyday numbers. Open Characters & writing to watch and practise the five characters below.
一 yī — one · 二 èr — two · 三 sān — three · 四 sì — four · 五 wǔ — five
Read the example words and their glossary. Listen, watch each character once, trace it, then try copying. Hide the model for recall when you feel ready.

sources.title: Hanzi Writer Data 2.0.1 / Make Me a Hanzi

notes.explanation: 一个 (yí ge): one; a single item. Draw left to right in one continuous movement.
二月 (èr yuè): February. Write the shorter upper stroke before the longer lower stroke.
三个 (sān ge): three items. Write from top to bottom; keep the bottom stroke longest.
四月 (sì yuè): April. Finish the inside before closing the bottom of the frame.
五个 (wǔ ge): five items. Watch how the third stroke turns; it is one stroke.
六月 (liù yuè): June. Keep the two lower strokes separated.
七月 (qī yuè): July. The turning stroke stays continuous through the bend.
八个 (bā ge): eight items. Start the left falling stroke before the right falling stroke.
九月 (jiǔ yuè): September. Follow the second stroke around its bend without lifting.
十个 (shí ge): ten items. Write the horizontal before the vertical.
中国人 (Zhōngguó rén): Chinese person. The two strokes meet near the top. Compare with 入 rù (enter).
大学 (dàxué): university. Write the horizontal first, then the left falling stroke.
小学 (xiǎoxué): primary school. Write the centre first, then the left and right sides.
人口 (rénkǒu): population. The top and right side form one turning stroke.
日子 (rìzi): day; days. Put the inner horizontal in before closing the bottom.
一月 (yī yuè): January. Keep the inner horizontals inside the outer strokes.
喝水 (hē shuǐ): drink water. Keep the central stroke continuous to its hook.
火山 (huǒshān): volcano. Watch the order of the short upper strokes before the long ones.
木头 (mùtou): wood. Write the horizontal and vertical before the two falling strokes.
大山 (dà shān): a large mountain. Begin with the central upright; follow the model for the lower turn.
我们 (wǒmen): we; us. Follow the animated model; keep the long slanting hook continuous.
你好 (nǐ hǎo): hello. Finish the narrow left component before moving to the right.
好人 (hǎorén): a good person. Complete the left component before the right component.
中国 (Zhōngguó): China. Write the enclosure before the vertical running through it.
中国 (Zhōngguó): China. Write the inside, including its dot, before closing the frame.
学生 (xuésheng): student. Work from the upper part down to 子.
学生 (xuésheng): student. Notice where the vertical crosses the horizontal strokes.
吃饭 (chī fàn): eat; have a meal. Complete 口 first; keep the last turning stroke continuous.
喝茶 (hē chá): drink tea. Keep 口 narrow to leave room for the right component.
茶水 (cháshuǐ): tea; tea water. Complete the top component first and keep the lower part balanced.

characters.components: One horizontal stroke.
characters.tip: Draw left to right in one continuous movement.
characters.glossary: 个 ge: general counter. 一 changes tone in connected speech.

characters.components: Two horizontal strokes.
characters.tip: Write the shorter upper stroke before the longer lower stroke.
characters.glossary: 月 yuè: month; introduced later in this pilot.

characters.components: Three horizontal strokes.
characters.tip: Write from top to bottom; keep the bottom stroke longest.
characters.glossary: 个 ge: general counter; 人 rén: person.

characters.components: An enclosing frame with inner strokes.
characters.tip: Finish the inside before closing the bottom of the frame.
characters.glossary: 月 yuè: month.

characters.components: Horizontal strokes joined by a central structure.
characters.tip: Watch how the third stroke turns; it is one stroke.
characters.glossary: 个 ge: general counter; 人 rén: person.

characters.components: A top dot, a horizontal, and two lower strokes.
characters.tip: Keep the two lower strokes separated.
characters.glossary: 月 yuè: month.

characters.components: A horizontal and a turning stroke.
characters.tip: The turning stroke stays continuous through the bend.
characters.glossary: 月 yuè: month.

characters.components: Two strokes opening outwards.
characters.tip: Start the left falling stroke before the right falling stroke.
characters.glossary: 个 ge: general counter; 人 rén: person.

characters.components: A left falling stroke and a bent stroke with a hook.
characters.tip: Follow the second stroke around its bend without lifting.
characters.glossary: 月 yuè: month.

characters.components: A horizontal crossed by a vertical.
characters.tip: Write the horizontal before the vertical.
characters.glossary: 个 ge: general counter; 人 rén: person.

characters.components: A left falling and a right falling stroke.
characters.tip: The two strokes meet near the top. Compare with 入 rù (enter).
characters.glossary: 是 shì: am/is/are; 我 wǒ: I; 中国 Zhōngguó: China.

characters.components: A horizontal above two spreading strokes.
characters.tip: Write the horizontal first, then the left falling stroke.
characters.glossary: 很 hěn: very; often used before an adjective; 学 xué: study.

characters.components: A central hooked stroke with strokes on either side.
characters.tip: Write the centre first, then the left and right sides.
characters.glossary: 山 shān: mountain or hill; introduced later.

characters.components: A three-stroke enclosure.
characters.tip: The top and right side form one turning stroke.
characters.glossary: 口 kǒu can count family members in this expression.

characters.components: A rectangular enclosure with an inner horizontal.
characters.tip: Put the inner horizontal in before closing the bottom.
characters.glossary: 日 rì occurs in written dates and durations; 天 tiān is common in speech.

characters.components: A narrow outer form with two inner horizontals.
characters.tip: Keep the inner horizontals inside the outer strokes.
characters.glossary: A number followed by 月 names a month.

characters.components: A central hook with strokes on either side.
characters.tip: Keep the central stroke continuous to its hook.
characters.glossary: 我 wǒ: I; 喝 hē: drink.

characters.components: Two upper side strokes and two spreading lower strokes.
characters.tip: Watch the order of the short upper strokes before the long ones.
characters.glossary: 很 hěn: very; 大 dà: big.

characters.components: A horizontal, a central vertical and two spreading strokes.
characters.tip: Write the horizontal and vertical before the two falling strokes.
characters.glossary: 头 tou is unstressed in this word. 木 is also a common character component.

characters.components: Three upright parts joined at the base.
characters.tip: Begin with the central upright; follow the model for the lower turn.
characters.glossary: 很 hěn: very; 大 dà: big.

characters.components: A complex crossing structure including a 戈-like part.
characters.tip: Follow the animated model; keep the long slanting hook continuous.
characters.glossary: 文 wén: writing/language; 中文 Zhōngwén: Chinese; 学 xué: study.

characters.components: 亻 person component on the left; 尔 on the right.
characters.tip: Finish the narrow left component before moving to the right.
characters.glossary: In natural speech, the first third tone in 你好 changes to a rising tone.

characters.components: 女 on the left and 子 on the right.
characters.tip: Complete the left component before the right component.
characters.glossary: 你 nǐ: you; the greeting is a fixed expression. 好 also has other readings in other words.

characters.components: 口 crossed by a central vertical.
characters.tip: Write the enclosure before the vertical running through it.
characters.glossary: 国 guó: country; 很 hěn: very.

characters.components: An enclosing 囗 around 玉.
characters.tip: Write the inside, including its dot, before closing the frame.
characters.glossary: 我 wǒ: I; 是 shì: am; 人 rén: person.

characters.components: Upper short strokes, a cover, and 子 below.
characters.tip: Work from the upper part down to 子.
characters.glossary: 我 wǒ: I; 是 shì: am; 生 sheng is unstressed in 学生.

characters.components: An upper falling stroke over a vertical and horizontals.
characters.tip: Notice where the vertical crosses the horizontal strokes.
characters.glossary: 你 nǐ: you; 是 shì: are; 学生 xuésheng: student.

characters.components: 口 on the left and 乞 on the right.
characters.tip: Complete 口 first; keep the last turning stroke continuous.
characters.glossary: 饭 fàn: cooked rice or meal; recognition-only vocabulary.

characters.components: 口 on the left with a larger right component.
characters.tip: Keep 口 narrow to leave room for the right component.
characters.glossary: 你 nǐ: you; 茶 chá: tea.

characters.components: 艹 at the top, with central and lower strokes.
characters.tip: Complete the top component first and keep the lower part balanced.
characters.glossary: 我 wǒ: I; 喝 hē: drink.
